analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, which is documentation only. The visible portion (head lines 1853-2291) holds historical release notes for v0.10.3, v0.10.2, v0.10.1 and v0.10.0. The patch adds a v0.10.8 candidate section near the top of the file, outside the supplied lines. That candidate text is truncated in the patch excerpt and not covered here.

The prose touches security-relevant areas:
- T-041: encrypted SSD prefix-cache checkpoints, namespaces and TTL sweep.
- Cache-routing allowlist and coordinator version floors.
- Desktop loopback control API and device-code login.
- Autopilot downloads, holds and adoption.
- A KV-backend guard that binds only the tripped version.

None of this describes executable code. No controls were changed, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated by these lines. The T-041 posture is unchanged in kind: the 4-bit balanced checkpoints use their own namespaces, expire through the existing TTL sweep, and are described as keeping the same encryption and HMAC scheme.

Remaining uncertainty: the actual source changes behind the v0.10.8 notes (pair update, cluster approvals, pair refusal on build mismatch) are not visible in these units. The truncated candidate section was not reviewed. Integration should examine the code diffs for those changes, including whether the cluster pair update path enforces authenticity and fail-closed behavior.
